pilot: review-work OUTPUT-FORMAT A/B: does re-adding an explicit review-output template (registry/review-work/references/review-output.md, dropped in the 92d0abd units-of-work rebuild) improve the structural conformance and consistency of review output over the current prose-only skill, WITHOUT costing defect recall or precision?
purpose: The current review-work skill describes the output in prose (review-protocol.md: 'return a verdict, a short reason, the validation run, and findings ordered by severity') but gives no skeleton to fill; the risk sub-mode kept its table template while the findings path lost its shape. This is a PRESENTATION change, so the review_ab recall/precision harness is the wrong instrument for its value — it is the right instrument for its cost. Here we measure conformance: does every review reliably carry a clear verdict token, a reviewer-model attribution line, a validation line, and severity-tagged findings, in a postable shape. Run review_ab in parallel as a no-regression guardrail.

arms.control: Current review-work skill (registry/review-work) with no delta. Prose-only output guidance.
arms.template: Control plus the review-output template delta (candidate re-add). Expected to raise conformance — especially the near-always-missing model-attribution line and consistent severity tagging — with no loss of recall/precision on the review_ab guardrail.

arm_deltas.template:
Present your review in exactly this shape. Verdict first, a tight summary, honest validation, then findings ordered by severity. This controls presentation only; what earns a finding is unchanged.

## Code Review

**Verdict: <APPROVE | REQUEST CHANGES | COMMENT>**
**Model: <exact id of the model that produced this review, e.g. claude-opus-4-8; "unknown" if not reliably known>**

<Two to four sentences: what you reviewed (scope), the one reason the verdict holds, and the bottom line. Do not narrate the change back to the author.>

### Validation

- <what you actually ran or inspected, with real results — one line each>

Then findings, most severe first, each as:

**<Blocking | Major | Minor | Nit>:** <problem>. <evidence>. <fix or precise question>.

If nothing is actionable, write "No actionable findings." and omit the list. The Model line is required and must carry a real identifier, not the placeholder. REQUEST CHANGES needs a Blocking finding (or a Major that makes merge unsafe); Minor and Nit never drive REQUEST CHANGES.

protocol: For each arm x case x rep, an answer agent reads registry/review-work/SKILL.md and its references, applies the arm delta (if any), and reviews the case intent+diff. A blind evaluator scores the REVIEW's structural conformance against fixed format anchors (verdict token, model line, validation section, severity-tagged findings, concise summary). Consistency is the across-rep variance of the conformance score per arm. Runs on review_format_ab.workflow.js. Smoke trial, not a statistical benchmark; preserve raw reviews.
metric: Per arm: mean conformance (fraction of the 5 format anchors satisfied) and its across-rep spread (lower spread = more consistent). Guardrail: run review_ab.workflow.js with the same two arms; template must not lower include-fraction on any target nor raise exclude-count.

gate.adopt_template_if: mean conformance(template) is clearly above control (driven especially by the model-attribution line and consistent severity tagging), AND the review_ab guardrail shows no recall drop on any target and no precision drop.
gate.keep_control_if: template does not raise conformance, or it regresses recall/precision on the guardrail. A null conformance result keeps the current prose-only skill.
